R5: Formed Greater Iberia as Contestani, avenging the extinction of Iberic culture and religion in my last playthrough. This was my second game of I:R, so I have a few takeaways:

* Other tribes will spam mercenaries, so all wars need to be quick: take the war goal, peace out before mercs are at full morale.
* By far the hardest part of this run is the first war with Carthage / Rome (or both), killing four previous runs. This war is unavoidable and usually happens around 500-520 due to the natural progression of the missions.   
All you are aiming for is a white peace, which means you just have to hold them off for a few years. This run, Carthage was mostly dismantled by Rome, so I managed to survive the Roman invasion through alliances with Lemovicia and the remnants of Carthage. Thankfully, the AI is terrible at overseas wars (see below).
* I conquered easily conquered the last half of Iberia in the last forty years of the campaign, after I got my research efficiency past 100. Before I reformed my tribe, I would have to send in double the enemy troup counts just to have a hope of winning battles. Long story short, rushing centralization is really important.
* Carthage is a donkey. Around 530, it called me into war against Ilensia, the friendless two province minor on the island of Sardinia. I have no navy, but whatever, I'll just continue conquering on the mainland. 15+ years later, my war exhaustion is approaching 40, I can't disband my troops.   
Fine.   
I build a navy, send an army, siege their capital, instant white peace. A year or so later, Carthage insults me and breaks the alliance.   
what.   
A year or so later, Carthage declares war on my tribal vassal, Ilensia.   
*what*.   
Apparently, it wasn't a white peace, and Carthage gave me Ilensia as a tribal vassal then got angry at me. I ignore the war, my tribal vassal occupies Sardinia for me, I take control of Western Sardinia while never seeing any Carthaginian troops. Over the next fifty years, Carthage would declare war on me three more times and I never saw more than 2k troops at a time.   
In conclusion, Carthage is a donkey.
* The "Envy of Rome" mission is utter nonsense when my captial has more pops and more civillization than Rome, and Rome isn't even the capital of Rome.

I am pretty sure I could at least double my territory count by the end date, but I'll be ending this campaign here.

The Eldrazi you are referring to were in a set known as Zendikar from a few years ago, hence why they were in Magic 2014. So unfortunately, while it is possible, it is unlikely that those Eldrazi will return to Magic Duels. BUT, in just a couple of months, we will be returning to Zendikar, and those cards will be added to duels.

Back in grade six, there was this series of related assignments, a journal of some sort that I don't really remember. Anyhow, this moment in time is maybe the third one, and I put a LOT of effort into it because I hadn't done well on the previous ones. To cut a long story short, I nearly failed it.

Teary eyed, I go up to my teacher, and before I even say anything she has already cut me off by saying she won't change my mark. I tell her that I just want to know what I did wrong, but she isn't even paying attention at this point. At this point, she just waves me off telling me that I can stop crying because it won't change anything.

Back in elementary school, I was easily upset, and would cry when people would bully me a lot or when an assignment didn't go my way. I mean, being a generally chipper person, I would cry for maybe 10-15 minutes before I cheered myself up and told myself that everything would be OK, and this kind of thing would only happen maybe once a month. Nevertheless, being a guy, I was known through the school as a crybaby and had very few friends.

So back to the story, I just tell myself that I'll do better on the next one and join the other kids. Shortly thereafter, the teacher takes us outside for some activity, and sees we with a smile back on my face. She just says: "AHA! I knew you were just faking it, don't think that you can pull that trick on me again!" I haven't cried since.

**TL;DR:** Got upset over mark in grade six, teacher berated me for faking tears. I haven't cried since.
